title: Fractions and Decimals: Parts of Wholes, Done Precisely

questions.question: Compute 3/4 + 5/6.
questions.rationale: The LCM of 4 and 6 is 12: 3/4 = 9/12 and 5/6 = 10/12, and 9/12 + 10/12 = 19/12 = 1 7/12. Adding denominators (giving 8/10) is the classic error the lesson warns against.

questions.question: Compute 3/4 ÷ 2/5.
questions.rationale: Dividing means multiplying by the reciprocal: 3/4 ÷ 2/5 = 3/4 × 5/2 = 15/8 = 1 7/8.

questions.question: Evaluate 15/8 × 4/9 by cancelling first.
questions.rationale: Cancel 15 with 9 (÷3) and 4 with 8 (÷4) before multiplying, leaving (5 × 1)/(2 × 3) = 5/6 — the same value as 60/72 but with no big products.

questions.question: Which fraction is less than the other: 3/7 or 3/5?
questions.rationale: With the same numerator, the larger denominator gives the smaller fraction — cutting a whole into 7 pieces makes each piece smaller than cutting it into 5.

questions.question: Which of these fractions gives a terminating decimal?
questions.rationale: A fraction terminates exactly when its denominator (in lowest terms) has only 2s and 5s as prime factors. 40 = 2³ × 5 qualifies, so 7/40 = 0.175 terminates; 12 (2² × 3), 9 (3²) and 3 all contain other primes.

questions.question: Convert the recurring decimal 0.777… to a fraction.
questions.rationale: Let x = 0.777…; then 10x = 7.777… and 10x − x = 7, so 9x = 7 and x = 7/9.

questions.question: Convert 0.232323… (23 repeating) to a fraction.
questions.rationale: For a two-digit repeat, shift by 100: 100x − x = 23.2323… − 0.2323… = 23, so 99x = 23 and x = 23/99.

questions.question: Compute 0.3 × 0.02.
questions.rationale: Multiply 3 × 2 = 6, then plant as many decimal places as the factors had combined: 1 + 2 = 3 places, giving 0.006.

questions.question: Round 3.4567 to two decimal places.
questions.rationale: Inspect the third decimal digit (6); since 6 ≥ 5, round the second digit up: 3.4567 → 3.46.

questions.question: Using the fraction–decimal table, what is 5/8 as a decimal?
questions.rationale: 5/8 = 4/8 + 1/8 = 0.5 + 0.125 = 0.625, exactly as derived in the lesson's conversion table.
